title: Pixels and alpha
description:
Work with 32-bit BGRA pixels like WIC and Direct2D do:

```cpp
struct Pixel { std::uint8_t b, g, r, a; };
struct RectF { float left, top, right, bottom; };

Pixel premultiply(Pixel straight);       // c * a / 255, rounded to nearest
Pixel unpremultiply(Pixel p);            // c * 255 / a, rounded to nearest, capped at 255; a == 0 gives all zero
Pixel over(Pixel src, Pixel dst);        // premultiplied "source over": src + dst * (255 - src.a) / 255, rounded
RectF fit(float w, float h, RectF box);  // contain: largest same-shape rectangle inside box, centred
RectF fill(float w, float h, RectF box); // cover: smallest same-shape rectangle covering box, centred
std::vector<Pixel> halve(const std::vector<Pixel>& image, int w, int h);   // 2x2 box filter; w and h even
```

Rounding to nearest for integer division by `d`: `(x + d / 2) / d`. `halve` averages each 2 × 2 block channel by channel (premultiplied pixels, so alpha is averaged like the others), rounding to nearest: `(sum + 2) / 4`.
hints: `(c * a + 127) / 255` is "c times a divided by 255, rounded to nearest" in integers; the same pattern with `a / 2` works for dividing by `a`.
